AI.tldr: CGMas automates polymer coarse-graining via a multi-agent LLM-based workflow, inferring AA topology from polymer name, automatic mapping, Boltzmann-inversion potentials, equilibration, and validation. Achieves 27 polymer tasks with high density accuracy and dramatic speedup.
AI.motivation: Bottom-up coarse-grained (CG) modeling is laborious and lacks transferable parameters across mappings; automation is needed to generalize CG construction for polymers.
AI.method: CGMas employs a multi-agent framework: an LLM reasoning agent infers the atomistic topology from polymer name; layered self-correction fixes issues typical of unsaturated, heteroatom-containing, and polar polymers. Downstream agents perform equilibration, map to CG representation, derive CG potentials via Boltzmann inversion, and benchmark against the atomistic reference.
AI.result: Completed 27 homopolymer and copolymer tasks; matched atomistic density within 5% for 22 tasks; reduced simulation time from 38–88 minutes to 1 minute per task.
AI.conclusion: Agentic LLM-driven automation enables automated polymer coarse-graining at scale, delivering accurate density reproduction and substantial time savings across diverse polymer systems.

title: Theoretical Foundations of Communication-Efficient, Robust, and Practical Distributed and Federated Optimization
summary: Machine learning and optimization have advanced together, with practical demands motivating new theory and theoretical breakthroughs enabling new applications. Modern large-scale training relies on classical optimization principles, but the constraints of distributed systems require these foundations to be reconsidered. This thesis addresses seven challenges at the intersection of theory and practice, focusing on key bottlenecks in federated learning and distributed optimization. First, we introduce ProxSkip and prove that local gradient steps can accelerate communication, providing a theoretical foundation for this widely used heuristic. Second, we develop Variance Reduced ProxSkip, which eliminates the neighborhood error of stochastic local updates while balancing communication and local computation. Third, we show that local steps retain their communication acceleration under partial client participation. Fourth, we prove that server-side stepsizes and sampling without replacement improve convergence in heterogeneous settings. Fifth, for Random Reshuffling, we demonstrate that compressing gradient differences rather than gradients yields better theoretical and practical performance. Sixth, we establish that Byzantine robustness and partial participation can be achieved simultaneously using gradient-difference clipping. Finally, we develop the first theoretical framework for low-rank adaptation based on randomized asymmetric chains, providing new insights into fine-tuning large models. Across these contributions, we introduce novel algorithmic frameworks, establish sharp guarantees under realistic assumptions, and support the theory with numerical experiments.

AI.tldr: A seven-part thesis that advances distributed optimization for federated learning through ProxSkip-based acceleration, variance reduction, robustness, and a novel low-rank adaptation framework, with rigorous guarantees and experiments.
AI.motivation: To reconcile classical optimization with distributed ML constraints, addressing bottlenecks such as communication efficiency, heterogeneity, robustness, and scalable fine-tuning of large models.
AI.method: Develop and analyze seven algorithmic components: ProxSkip; Variance Reduced ProxSkip; local steps under partial client participation; server-side stepsizes and sampling without replacement; gradient-difference compression for Random Reshuffling; gradient-difference clipping for Byzantine robustness; randomized asymmetric chains for low-rank adaptation.
AI.result: Provide sharp convergence guarantees under realistic assumptions; improved communication efficiency; reduced neighborhood errors; robustness with partial participation; practical improvements validated by experiments.
AI.conclusion: Presents the first theoretical framework for low-rank adaptation via randomized asymmetric chains and delivers multiple algorithmic frameworks with strong theoretical guarantees, bridging theory and practice in federated/distributed ML.

title: Benchmarking and Reasoning Distillation of Large Language Models for Feedback Controller Design in Complex Dynamical Systems
summary: Although remarkable capabilities have been demonstrated by Large Language Models (LLMs) across scientific domains, feedback controller design remains underexplored. Existing benchmarks focus mainly on linear single-Degree-of-Freedom (DoF) systems and large API-hosted models, leaving performance on complex controller-design tasks and feasibility for edge deployment unclear. To address these limitations, we introduce the Complex Dynamics-to-Control Benchmark for Large Language Models (CoDyControlBench), comprising 132 system configurations across five evaluation dimensions: number of DoF, system type, coupling level, damping regime, and controller type. Six state-of-the-art LLMs were evaluated over three independent runs, including three commercial models (GPT, Gemini, and Claude) and three open-source models (GLM, DeepSeek, and Qwen). GPT achieved the highest design success rate at 94.8\%, whereas Qwen showed the lowest rate at 50.0\%. Across the benchmark dimensions, DoF and controller type exhibited the largest model-averaged variations in design success, with success-rate ranges of 36.3\% and 17.6\%, respectively, exceeding those associated with system type, coupling level, and damping regime. Comparison of GPT and Qwen showed that their performance gap arose mainly from the control-design knowledge, particularly gain selection and the use of transient-limiting mechanisms. For edge deployment, a specialized 1.5B-parameter model was developed through reasoning distillation. The reasoning-distilled model outperformed the answer-distilled and base model on CoDyControlBench, maintained stable performance across 1-6 DoFs, and achieved successful traget tracking in all three physical trials on a pneumatic-artificial-muscle-driven robotic arm. These results establish a benchmark baseline and highlight the potential of lightweight, edge-deployable controller-design models.

AI.tldr: CoDyControlBench introduces a 132-configuration benchmark for LLM-based controller design across five dimensions (DoF, system type, coupling, damping, controller type), evaluating six LLMs and highlighting DoF/controller type as major performance drivers. A 1.5B reasoning-distilled model enables effective edge deployment and reliable physical-trial tracking on a pneumatic-artificial-muscle robotic arm.
AI.motivation: Address the gap that LLMs' controller-design capabilities are underexplored, limiting benchmarks to linear single-DoF systems and API-hosted models, and to assess edge-deployable solutions.
AI.method: Construct CoDyControlBench with 132 configurations across five axes (DoF, system type, coupling level, damping regime, controller type); evaluate six LLMs (GPT, Gemini, Claude, GLM, DeepSeek, Qwen) over three runs; compare reasoning-distilled edge model (1.5B) against answer-distilled and base models; validate with three physical trials on a pneumatic-artificial-muscle robotic arm.
AI.result: GPT achieved 94.8% design success; Qwen 50.0%; DoF and controller type yield the largest model-averaged variation in success (36.3% and 17.6%). Performance gap between GPT and Qwen linked to control-design knowledge (gain selection, transient-limiting). Edge-distilled 1.5B model outperformed answer-distilled and base across CoDyControlBench, remained stable 1-6 DoFs, and achieved successful target tracking in all three trials on a pneumatic-artificial-muscle-driven arm.
AI.conclusion: Establishes a benchmark baseline for complex dynamics-to-control tasks, demonstrates the feasibility of lightweight, edge-deployable controller-design models, and identifies DoF and controller type as key levers for LLM performance in control design.

title: UniCycleFlow: Bidirectional Unpaired Image Translation with a Shared Rectified Flow
summary: Bidirectional unpaired image translation must preserve source-specific structure while learning coherent transformations in both directions without paired supervision. Existing methods typically employ two direction-specific generators or train separate one-way models. Even when linked by cycle consistency, such models constrain only the round-trip endpoint reconstruction, without requiring the two directions to obey a common local transformation rule. We propose UniCycleFlow, a rectified-flow framework that represents bidirectional translation as forward and reverse integration of a single time-conditioned velocity field. This formulation organizes both directions within the same continuous dynamics, rather than coupling otherwise separate endpoint mappings. A key challenge is that unpaired data provide no meaningful source--target coupling from which rectified-flow trajectories can be constructed. UniCycleFlow addresses this challenge by learning deterministic source-conditioned endpoints whose marginal distributions are adversarially matched to the opposite domains. The resulting paths are regularized by stop-gradient self-flow matching for intermediate velocity supervision, discrete cycle closure for forward--reverse consistency, and representation path-velocity regularization for controlling localized feature changes along the trajectory. Across ten translation directions, UniCycleFlow achieves the lowest FID on 7 of 10 tasks using a single Euler evaluation and obtains the best average FID of 55.1.

AI.tldr: UniCycleFlow unifies bidirectional unpaired image translation as forward and reverse integration of a single time-conditioned velocity field (rectified flow). It learns source-conditioned endpoints with adversarially matched marginals and uses multiple regularizations to enforce consistency and localized changes, achieving strong FID performance across 10 directions with a single Euler step.
AI.motivation: Existing bidirectional translation methods either use two separate generators or rely on cycle consistency, which only enforces endpoint round-trips and does not enforce a common local transformation rule. A single continuous dynamics that governs both directions can better preserve source-structure while enabling coherent bidirectional transformations.
AI.method: A rectified-flow framework representing translation as forward/reverse integration of one velocity field conditioned on time. Learns deterministic source-conditioned endpoints whose marginals are adversarially matched to the opposite domains. Regularized by stop-gradient self-flow matching for intermediate velocity supervision, discrete cycle closure for forward–reverse consistency, and representation path-velocity regularization to control localized feature changes. Evaluation uses a single Euler step.
AI.result: Across ten translation directions, UniCycleFlow achieves the lowest FID on 7 of 10 tasks and attains the best average FID of 55.1.
AI.conclusion: The approach demonstrates that unifying bidirectional translation under a single rectified-flow dynamic with endpoint learning and targeted regularizations yields improved quality and consistency across multiple directions using unpaired data.

title: AgentPatch: Coarse-to-Fine Weak-Task Repair for Merging Agentic Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: Agentic multimodal large language models (MLLMs) extend multimodal perception and reasoning with planning, tool use, and interaction in dynamic environments. Yet current models are specialized for particular tools or environments, complicating consolidation into a single generalist. We formulate Agentic MLLM Merging and identify two challenges: asymmetric capability preservation, whereby capabilities with different interaction complexity are retained unevenly, producing weak tasks after merging, and behavior-critical forgetting, whereby losing decisive actions can derail long-horizon execution. We propose AgentPatch, a training-free coarse-to-fine repair framework. It selects a stable merged backbone, restores diluted weak-task-specific signals through Weak-Task Unique Residual Recovery, and applies an Agent-Guided Behavior-Critical Patch that recovers decisive behaviors under explicit capability protection. AgentPatch produces a single static checkpoint without routing or ensembles. Experiments across six agentic and multimodal benchmarks show that AgentPatch improves diverse merged backbones, alleviates weak-task degradation, and better balances weak-task recovery with the preservation of complementary search and agentic visual processing capabilities. Code is available at https://github.com/ziboshao/AgentPatch.

AI.tldr: AgentPatch is a training-free, coarse-to-fine repair framework that merges agentic multimodal LLM backbones into a single static checkpoint, addressing asymmetric capability preservation and behavior-critical forgetting by (1) selecting a stable merged backbone, (2) Weak-Task Unique Residual Recovery, and (3) Agent-Guided Behavior-Critical Patch; demonstrated across six benchmarks with improvements.
AI.motivation: Merging disparate agentic MLLMs into a single generalist is hampered by asymmetric retention of capabilities and forgetting decisive actions; a training-free solution is desirable to avoid retraining complexity and maintain efficiency.
AI.method: A three-stage repair pipeline: backbone selection from merged models; restoration of weak-task signals via Weak-Task Unique Residual Recovery; behavior-critical patching to recover decisive actions under explicit capability protection; results in a single static checkpoint without routing or ensembles.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on six benchmarks shows improved performance of merged backbones, reduced weak-task degradation, and better balance between weak-task recovery and preservation of search and agentic visual processing capabilities; code released.
AI.conclusion: AgentPatch offers a practical, training-free approach to robustly merge agentic MLLMs into a generalist, mitigating key failure modes and yielding a compact, static model with broad capabilities.

title: Quantization Damage Is Multiplicative, Not Additive
comment: 16 pages, 9 figures, 7 tables. Under review at the Third Workshop on Uncertainty-Aware NLP (UncertaiNLP), EMNLP 2026 (non-archival)
summary: Quantization is how large language models are actually deployed, and below four bits it is known to hurt. What nobody can say is which of the model's decisions will change at a given bit-width. The damage is silent: a compressed agent stops calling its tools, then loses half its safety refusals, yet benchmark scores barely move. Prior work assumes quantization adds noise of a roughly fixed size, which would make confident decisions safe. We measure the decision itself instead. The margin of a two-way decision is the model's score for the option it picks minus the score of its best alternative; we track it before and after quantization across 16 models from 8 model families, three quantization methods, and bit-widths from 8 down to 2. Quantization does not add fixed-size noise to the margin. It multiplies the margin by a factor that collapses with bit-width (median 0.86 at 4 bits, 0.33 at 3, 0.00 at 2); we call this margin shrinkage. This contraction reduces the protection a large margin affords; the model's own small biases pick the direction of failure: at 3 bits the decision to call a tool collapses toward inaction while the choice of which tool is untouched. In fitted statistical comparison, additive-noise accounts never win on the damaged tool and safety decisions. The fitted relation predicts flip rates within a median of 1.8 percentage points on held-out decisions, though no flip was used in the fit; per decision, the predicted flip probabilities are calibrated uncertainty estimates (expected calibration error 0.004 over 131,758 predictions). The same form holds in every model we measure, but the constants are each model's own and do not transfer. A small paired margin set, measured per model and bit-width, estimates which decisions break without full generative evaluation; under our cost-matched tests, nothing repairs damage more cheaply than one more bit.

AI.tldr: Quantization at low bit-widths distorts decision margins rather than adding uniform noise, causing higher-rate failures in tool-use safety decisions. Margin shrinkage (width-dependent attenuation of decision margins) predicts flips surprisingly well, is model-specific, and cannot be transferred. Increasing bit-width remains the most effective repair.
AI.motivation: Understand how aggressive quantization affects the internal decision dynamics of LLMs, especially which decisions break, to inform deployment safety and model compression strategies.
AI.method: Empirical study across 16 models from 8 families, 3 quantization methods, bit-widths 8→2. Measure two-way decision margins (chosen option score minus best alternative) before/after quantization. Define and quantify 'margin shrinkage' as the multiplicative factor on margins. Compare additive-noise vs margin-based predictions of flips. Calibrate flip probabilities; evaluate held-out decisions. Use per-model, per-bit-width margin subsets to predict which decisions break. Cost-matched tests compare repair by bit-width increase.
AI.result: Quantization multiplies rather than adds fixed noise to margins. Margin shrinkage factors: median 0.86 at 4 bits, 0.33 at 3 bits, 0.00 at 2 bits. At 3 bits, tool-calling decisions collapse toward inaction while the tool-choice remains mostly intact. Additive-noise models fail to predict damaged-tool flips; a margin-based fit predicts flip rates within ~1.8 percentage points on held-out data, with well-calibrated probabilities (ECE ~0.004 over 131k predictions). Constants differ by model and do not transfer. A small per-model margin subset suffices to anticipate breakage. Across cost-matched tests, adding capacity (one more bit) is the most effective repair.
AI.conclusion: Low-bit quantization degrades decision safety via margin shrinkage, not fixed noise; model behavior becomes dominated by its small biases. Margins, not noise, determine which decisions fail. Deployment guidance: rely on higher bit-width or model-specific margin calibration; uniform transfer of findings across models is unlikely.

title: Real-time Whole-Body Motion Planning for Mobile Manipulators Carrying Arbitrarily Shaped Payloads via Kinematically-Coupled SVSDF
summary: Mobile manipulators are increasingly tasked with transporting large, non-convex payloads through cluttered environments, yet existing planners either oversimplify the payload geometry or fail to handle the kinematic coupling between manipulator links, leading to lost feasible space or stalled optimization. This letter presents a real-time whole-body motion planning framework for mobile manipulators carrying arbitrarily shaped payloads. The front-end employs a chain-decomposed kernel-based collision check that preserves the true geometry of the robot and payload, with compact storage and fast bit-level queries. A mid-end preprocessing stage converts the front-end path into a continuous trajectory enforcing smoothness and feasibility, and executes it directly when collision-free to bypass the costly back-end. When refinement is required, the back-end performs trajectory optimization built on a Kinematically-Coupled SVSDF (KC-SVSDF), which propagates collision-avoidance gradients along the kinematic chain to produce coherent whole-body escape directions. Ablation studies, comparative benchmarks against state-of-the-art baselines, and real-world experiments on a differential-drive mobile manipulator demonstrate that the proposed framework reliably transports large, non-convex payloads through tight passages and cluttered environments.

AI.tldr: A real-time whole-body motion planning framework for mobile manipulators carrying arbitrarily shaped payloads, combining a chain-decomposed kernel-based collision checker, mid-end trajectory smoothing, and a back-end KC-SVSDF-based optimization to handle kinematic coupling and complex payload geometries.
AI.motivation: Existing mobile-manipulator planners either oversimplify payload geometry or neglect kinematic coupling among links, causing loss of feasible space or stalled optimization in cluttered environments. A need exists for geometry-faithful, real-time, whole-body planning that can transport large, non-convex payloads.
AI.method: Front-end: chain-decomposed kernel-based collision checking that preserves true robot-payload geometry with compact storage and fast bit-level queries. Mid-end: preprocesses the front-end path into a continuous, smooth, feasible trajectory and can execute collision-free paths directly to bypass the back-end. Back-end: trajectory optimization using Kinematically-Coupled SVSDF (KC-SVSDF) to propagate collision-avoidance gradients along the kinematic chain, producing coherent whole-body escape directions.
AI.result: Ablation studies and benchmarks against state-of-the-art baselines, plus real-world experiments on a differential-drive mobile manipulator, demonstrate reliable transportation of large, non-convex payloads through tight passages and clutter.
AI.conclusion: The framework enables real-time, coherent whole-body motion planning for mobile manipulators with arbitrarily shaped payloads in cluttered environments by preserving payload geometry, respecting kinematic coupling, and providing efficient front-end processing with a KC-SVSDF-based back-end when refinement is needed.

title: PAST: Prompt-Adaptive Sampling Termination for Efficient Diffusion Model
summary: While diffusion models have made significant progress in text-to-image tasks, they still exhibit limitations when directly optimizing downstream objectives. Although Reinforcement Learning (RL) enables targeted optimization, existing methods are generally constrained by low-efficiency fine-tuning and sparse rewards. To address these challenges, we propose PAST, which provides differentiated rewards while adaptively regulating training episode length by jointly perceiving denoising progress and prompt difficulty. Specifically, we design an intrinsic reward paradigm to compensate for sparse extrinsic rewards and guide the model to explore paths that diverge more efficiently from noise patterns. We further provide theoretical justification for intrinsic rewards. Then, PAST dynamically monitors denoising completion and semantic alignment between image structures and prompt semantics. When both metrics satisfy generation requirements, the system adaptively terminates training. This enables appropriate allocation of episode lengths based on prompt difficulty and the current generation process. Finally, based on the predicted residual noise level, we establish a dual adaptive coordination mechanism. Specifically, it not only balances the extrinsic and intrinsic rewards but also balances the exploration and convergence. Experimental results demonstrate that PAST enhances computational efficiency of existing RL fine-tuning methods by up to 66.7%, while improving preference optimization quality by up to 29.5% through its dual adaptive regulation mechanism.

AI.tldr: PAST introduces intrinsic rewards and adaptive episode control to RL-fine-tune diffusion models, balancing exploration and convergence. It monitors denoising progress and semantic alignment to terminate episodes and uses residual-noise-based coordination, yielding major efficiency gains (~66.7%) and better preference optimization (~29.5%).
AI.motivation: Diffusion models struggle with directly optimizing downstream objectives due to sparse rewards and inefficient fine-tuning. RL offers targeted optimization but tends to be slow and brittle. There is a need for efficient, reward-informed exploration and adaptive training lengths.
AI.method: Introduce an intrinsic reward paradigm to supplement sparse extrinsic rewards. Jointly monitor denoising progress and prompt semantic alignment to adaptively terminate training episodes. Implement a dual adaptive coordination mechanism based on predicted residual noise to balance extrinsic/intrinsic rewards and exploration/convergence.
AI.result: Experiments show up to 66.7% improvement in computational efficiency of RL fine-tuning methods and up to 29.5% improvement in preference optimization quality, attributed to dual adaptive regulation and intrinsic rewards.
AI.conclusion: PAST provides a principled RL-based framework for diffusion-model fine-tuning that uses intrinsic rewards and adaptive episode control to improve efficiency and optimization quality; the approach is supported by theoretical justification of intrinsic rewards and demonstrated gains.

title: WebRider: Persona-Conditioned Intent Controllers for Live-Web Assistance
summary: Delegating a web task involves more than asking a question; it requires transferring a policy: what to verify, how to handle uncertainty, which preferences matter, and when to stop. Yet, current live-web agents are evaluated solely on the final answer, ignoring the policy constraints that define the delegation. A plausible final answer can conceal violations of that policy. Our full live audit reveals this critical gap: a strong controller completes 99.2% of tasks but honors all policy constraints in only 38.8% of cases. Finishing does not imply fidelity. WebRider bridges this gap by formalizing the delegated policy as an intent contract---an operational record of goals, constraints, evidence obligations, answer form, and task-local persona controls that must hold even as web pages change. WebRider employs a hierarchical architecture: a top-layer controller maintains the contract, a middle layer realizes intentions as guarded executable actions, and a tool layer executes these actions via browser, search, and maps tools. Our benchmark, RiderBench, evaluates this design on 4,096 live-web contracts across 42 public websites, auditing both the internal contract state and the visible user experience to determine if a rollout preserved its policy and if the steps were persona-consistent. The guarded middle interface also serves as a high-quality training signal; an 8B action-policy model trained through this interface outperforms executable-only baselines under a fixed controller. By making the browsing path a first-class object, WebRider enables a system that is auditable, human-judgeable, and learnable without conflating action realization with final-answer decisions. Dataset URL: hf.co/datasets/WebRider/WebRider.

AI.tldr: WebRider introduces an intent-contract policy framework for live-web agents with a three-layer architecture (controller, guarded actions, and tools). It shows a gap between task completion and policy fidelity, introducing RiderBench (4,096 contracts across 42 sites) and an 8B-action-policy model trained via a guarded interface that outperforms baselines. The dataset is released for auditable, human-judgeable, and learnable browsing paths.
AI.motivation: Current evaluations of live-web agents focus on final answers, ignoring the underlying policy constraints that govern delegation. This can allow high-quality answers to mask policy violations. A formal, auditable policy representation is needed to ensure fidelity to constraints, evidence obligations, and persona controls.
AI.method: Formulate policy as an intent contract detailing goals, constraints, evidence obligations, answer format, and task-local persona controls. Propose a hierarchical architecture: top-layer controller maintains the contract, middle-layer realizes intentions as guarded executable actions, and a tool layer executes actions via browser/search/maps tools. Validate via RiderBench (4,096 contracts across 42 sites), auditing internal contract state and user experience to assess policy preservation and persona-consistency. Use the guarded interface as a training signal to learn an 8B action-policy model that outperforms executable-only baselines under a fixed controller.
AI.result: The evaluation shows a large gap between task completion and policy fidelity: a strong controller completes 99.2% of tasks but honors policy constraints in only 38.8% of cases. The guarded middle interface enables a high-quality training signal, with an 8B action-policy model trained on this interface outperforming executable-only baselines under a fixed controller.
AI.conclusion: Policy fidelity must be evaluated alongside final answers. By making the browsing path a first-class object, WebRider achieves auditable, human-judgeable, and learnable behavior, decoupling action realization from final decision. The dataset (WebRider) enables broader benchmarking and development of policy-aware live-web agents.

title: CrystalGRPO: Target-Aligned and Coverage-Preserving Reinforcement Learning for Flow-Based Crystal Structure Prediction
summary: Flow-based generative models can efficiently produce candidate structures for crystal structure prediction (CSP), but their pretrained objectives do not directly optimize downstream target recovery. Reinforcement-learning post-training offers a flexible solution, yet existing approaches rely primarily on energy rewards and coordinate-only stochastic policies. Predicted energy does not identify the reference polymorph, while reward-driven concentration can reduce the candidate coverage required for Top-N recovery. We introduce CrystalGRPO, a CSP-aligned post-training framework that extends existing ODE-to-SDE policy constructions to the joint coordinate--lattice state. CrystalGRPO combines MACE-predicted energy with a StructureMatcher-based recovery score and provides two operating modes: CrystalGRPO-Q, which prioritizes single-draw recovery, and CrystalGRPO-C, which combines full-trajectory reference regularization with a coverage-aware group advantage to preserve finite-budget target recovery. Across MP-20 and MPTS-52 with PXRDGen and OMatG backbones, both variants reduce one- and twenty-sample RMSE relative to coordinate-only reinforcement in all four backbone--dataset settings. CrystalGRPO-Q consistently improves Top-1, whereas CrystalGRPO-C achieves a higher Top-20 across all settings.

AI.tldr: CrystalGRPO is a CSP-aligned RL post-training framework that jointly optimizes coordinates and lattice state for flow-based generative models, combining MACE-predicted energy with a StructureMatcher-based recovery score. It has two modes: CrystalGRPO-Q (single-draw recovery) and CrystalGRPO-C (trajectory regularization with coverage-aware group advantage). It improves RMSE across backbone/dataset settings and enhances Top-1 and Top-20 recovery metrics.
AI.motivation: To directly optimize downstream target (structure recovery) in CSP using RL post-training, addressing limitations of energy-only rewards and coordinate-only policies.
AI.method: Extend ODE-to-SDE policy constructions to joint coordinate-lattice state; integrate MACE-predicted energy with StructureMatcher-based recovery; two operating modes: CrystalGRPO-Q and CrystalGRPO-C; evaluate on MP-20 and MPTS-52 with PXRDGen and OMatG backbones; measure RMSE and Top-N recovery.
AI.result: Across MP-20 and MPTS-52 with PXRDGen and OMatG backbones, CrystalGRPO-Q and CrystalGRPO-C reduce 1- and 20-sample RMSE relative to coordinate-only RL in all four backbone-dataset settings; CrystalGRPO-Q improves Top-1 consistently; CrystalGRPO-C achieves higher Top-20 across settings.
AI.conclusion: Joint coordinate-lattice RL post-training with recovery-focused objectives yields better target recovery and coverage under finite budgets, outperforming coordinate-only RL baselines and offering mode-specific gains in Top-N recovery.

title: C2Dex: Contact-Consistent Reconstruction and Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Monocular Video
comment: 9 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L). Project page: https://k-jie.github.io/C2Dex/
summary: High-quality demonstrations for dexterous robot manipulation are costly and difficult to collect, whereas monocular human videos provide a scalable source of diverse manipulation behaviors. However, transferring such demonstrations to dexterous robots remains challenging: monocular hand-object interaction (HOI) reconstruction often produces temporally unstable contacts and physically implausible interactions, while conventional retargeting methods struggle to preserve task-relevant contacts and local interaction geometry across different hand embodiments. We present C2Dex, a video-to-dexterous-manipulation framework built around a shared interaction representation: stable object-side contacts recovered by aggregating noisy frame-wise observations in the canonical object space. These stable contacts serve a dual role: as trajectory-level constraints that guide reconstruction toward temporally coherent and physically plausible human HOI trajectories, and as explicit transfer targets for the dexterous hand, where Laplacian interaction optimization preserves the local hand-object geometry across embodiments and residual reinforcement learning refines the trajectory in simulation. Experiments on DexYCB and TACO show that C2Dex achieves end-to-end trajectory success rates of 57.78% and 26.67%, respectively, substantially outperforming the strongest baselines (17.78% and 10.00%) under identical evaluation criteria. Real-robot replay experiments further demonstrate physical feasibility across diverse contact-rich manipulation tasks. Project page: https://k-jie.github.io/C2Dex/

AI.tldr: C2Dex converts monocular human manipulation videos into actionable dexterous-robot trajectories using a shared interaction representation of stable object-side contacts. It couples contact-based reconstruction constraints with Laplacian geometry preservation and residual RL to transfer to dexterous hands, achieving substantially higher end-to-end trajectory success on DexYCB (57.78%) and TACO (26.67%) than baselines (17.78%, 10%), with real-robot validation.
AI.motivation: Monocular HOI videos provide scalable data but yield temporally unstable and physically implausible contacts when reconstructed for dexterous robots. Conventional retargeting fails to preserve task-relevant contacts and local geometry across hand embodiments, hindering transfer.
AI.method: C2Dex constructs a shared interaction representation by aggregating frame-wise observations into a canonical object space to recover stable object-side contacts. These contacts act as (1) trajectory-level constraints to enforce temporally coherent, physically plausible HOI trajectories, and (2) explicit transfer targets for the dexterous hand. The method uses Laplacian interaction optimization to preserve local hand–object geometry across embodiments and residual reinforcement learning to refine the trajectory in simulation. End-to-end replay on real hardware demonstrates feasibility.
AI.result: On DexYCB and TACO, C2Dex achieves end-to-end trajectory success rates of 57.78% and 26.67%, respectively, substantially higher than baselines (17.78% and 10%). Real-robot experiments confirm physical feasibility across diverse contact-rich tasks.
AI.conclusion: A shared object-space interaction representation coupled with geometry-preserving transfer enables effective monocular-to-dexterous manipulation transfer, improving success rates and enabling real-robot execution across diverse tasks.

title: AdvTiles: Physical Adversarial Camouflage Clothing against Person Detectors via Learnable Tiles
summary: Physical adversarial attacks against person detectors have evolved from localized patches to full-body textures. However, achieving both visual naturalness and strong attack effectiveness remains challenging. Existing natural-looking methods typically optimize camouflage textures as a whole, limiting the flexibility to refine local adversarial patterns and their spatial arrangement. To address this issue, we propose AdvTiles, a physical adversarial camouflage framework built from learnable tiles, enabling strong attack performance while preserving a natural camouflage appearance. Specifically, we use a Straight-through (ST) Gumbel-Softmax estimator for differentiable tile selection, enabling joint optimization of tile patterns and spatial layouts. This design provides fine-grained control over adversarial texture generation. To improve robustness in diverse physical conditions, we further optimize the camouflage through differentiable 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering with variations in viewpoints, scales, illuminations and backgrounds. Extensive experiments across multiple detectors demonstrate that AdvTiles achieves an average ASR of 86.2%, outperforming existing state-of-the-art attack methods. We further fabricate the optimized camouflage into wearable adversarial clothing, validating its effectiveness in real-world scenarios across diverse distances, angles and backgrounds.

AI.tldr: AdvTiles introduces a modular, differentiable tile-based camouflage framework for physical adversarial attacks on person detectors, using ST Gumbel-Softmax for tile selection and differentiable 3D Gaussian Splatting for robust rendering, achieving high attack success and demonstrably effective real-world wearables.
AI.motivation: To overcome the limitation of global camouflage textures that hinder local pattern refinement and spatial arrangement control, while maintaining natural appearance and robustness under real-world conditions.
AI.method: Construct learnable tiles forming the camouflage. Use Straight-through (ST) Gumbel-Softmax for differentiable tile selection to jointly optimize tile patterns and spatial layouts. Apply differentiable 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering with viewpoint, scale, illumination, and background variations to improve physical robustness. Validate by fabricating wearable camouflage clothing and testing across distances, angles, and backgrounds.
AI.result: Average Attack Success Rate (ASR) of 86.2% across multiple detectors, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Demonstrated effectiveness in real-world wearables across diverse distances, angles, and backgrounds.
AI.conclusion: Tile-based, differentiable camouflage enables fine-grained control over adversarial textures, balancing visual naturalness with attack effectiveness. The approach demonstrates practical viability through wearable deployment and robust performance under diverse physical conditions, with potential for broader applications and further refinements.

title: MolBioKG: Grounding Out-of-Graph Molecules in Biomedical Knowledge Graphs via Multi-Resolution Structural Anchoring
summary: Biomedical knowledge graphs (KGs) accelerate drug discovery, but standard pipelines assume query molecules already exist as graph entities, leaving unregistered molecules disconnected. We address this cold-start challenge, termed the out-of-graph molecule problem, by introducing MolBioKG. This two-layer system grounds unseen molecules in biomedical evidence via multi-resolution structural anchoring. It connects an index of 2.74 million molecules (represented by scaffolds, fragments, functional groups, and fingerprints) to a 9.6-million-edge KG. Given only a SMILES string, MolBioKG retrieves structurally related graph entities and traverses their biomedical neighborhoods without task-specific training. It features two inference mechanisms: static multi-anchor retrieval using Reciprocal Rank Fusion, and Adapt-KG, a tool-using LLM policy for adaptive traversal. Evaluated across in-graph link recovery, complex multi-hop reasoning, and out-of-graph generalization, MolBioKG outperforms strong baselines. Notably, it raises Hits@10 from 0.585 to 0.876 in multi-hop reasoning and out-of-graph target recall from 0.145 to 0.269, all while ensuring predictions retain traceable structural anchors and source-attributed KG evidence.

AI.tldr: A two-layer MolBioKG system addresses the out-of-graph molecule problem by grounding unseen molecules in biomedical evidence through structural anchoring, enabling retrieval and traversal without task-specific training.
AI.motivation: Biomedical knowledge graphs struggle with cold-start molecules; standard pipelines assume molecules exist as graph entities, leaving unseen compounds disconnected and hindering drug discovery.
AI.method: MolBioKG builds a two-layer framework: (1) a 2.74M-molecule index encoded via scaffolds, fragments, functional groups, and fingerprints linked to a 9.6M-edge KG; (2) two inference mechanisms—static multi-anchor retrieval using Reciprocal Rank Fusion and Adapt-KG, a tool-using LLM policy for adaptive graph traversal. Given a SMILES, it retrieves related graph entities and traverses their biomedical neighborhoods without task-specific training.
AI.result: MolBioKG improves in-graph link recovery, multi-hop reasoning, and out-of-graph generalization, e.g., Hits@10 rises from 0.585 to 0.876 in multi-hop reasoning and out-of-graph target recall from 0.145 to 0.269, outperforming strong baselines while keeping traceable structural anchors and source evidence.
AI.conclusion: The approach successfully grounds unseen molecules in biomedical evidence with traceable anchors, enabling robust reasoning and retrieval for out-of-graph molecules and integrating smoothly into drug discovery pipelines.

title: Flowing Through States: Neural ODE Regularization for Reinforcement Learning
summary: Neural networks applied to sequential decision-making tasks typically rely on latent representations of environment states. While environment dynamics dictate how semantic states evolve, the corresponding latent transitions are usually left implicit, creating a potential misalignment between the two. We propose to model latent dynamics explicitly by drawing an analogy between Markov decision process (MDP) trajectories and ordinary differential equation (ODE) flows: in both cases, the current state fully determines its successors. Building on this view, we introduce a neural ODE-based regularization method that enforces latent embeddings to follow consistent ODE flows, thereby aligning representation learning with environment dynamics. Although broadly applicable to deep learning agents, we demonstrate its effectiveness in reinforcement learning by integrating it into Actor-Critic algorithms. Our approach yields major performance gains across various standard Atari benchmarks for A2C and gridworld environments for PPO.

AI.tldr: A neural ODE–based regularization aligns latent dynamics with environment dynamics in RL, improving performance on Atari A2C and gridworld PPO.
AI.motivation: To fix potential misalignment between latent state transitions learned by neural networks and the true environment dynamics by enforcing explicit, consistent latent ODE flows.
AI.method: Model latent dynamics as neural ODE flows; regularize latent embeddings to follow these flows; integrate the regularizer into Actor-Critic RL algorithms; evaluate on Atari (A2C) and gridworld (PPO).
AI.result: Significant performance gains across standard Atari benchmarks for A2C and gridworld environments for PPO.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly regularizing latent dynamics via neural ODEs aligns representation learning with environment dynamics and yields substantial RL performance improvements.

title: AutoIntervene: Calibrated Intervention for Action-Chunking Imitation Learning Policies
summary: Action-chunking visuomotor policies learn from demonstrations and improve temporal consistency by predicting short action sequences rather than single-step commands. Yet perception errors and execution drift can move the robot outside the demonstration distribution, while the policy continues to produce smooth action chunks that are inconsistent with the observed state. We present AutoIntervene, an online framework that selectively transfers control between an action-chunking policy and an operator during deployment. AutoIntervene evaluates proposed chunks against a visual-action support memory built from successful task executions, combining visual similarity with consistency between proposed and reference actions. Phase-local support governs policy-to-operator transfer within the current task phase, whereas global support governs the return to policy control after operator recovery. We calibrate separate switching thresholds for the two directions from empirical quantiles of evaluation-level scores on held-out expert demonstrations, avoiding direct manual tuning of score cutoffs. Intervention segments retained from successful rollouts target learner-induced states and provide corrective supervision for subsequent policy updates. Experiments on real-world bimanual manipulation tasks show higher post-adaptation task success and lower operator-control time than manual intervention. Videos and additional results are available at https://aus.bot/research/autointervene/.

AI.tldr: AutoIntervene selectively hands control between an action-chunking visuomotor policy and a human operator using a visual-action support memory to maintain task performance under perception/execution drift.
AI.motivation: Perception errors and execution drift push states outside the demonstration distribution, causing autonomous policies to diverge from safe or successful behaviors; a principled intervention mechanism is needed to maintain performance without manual tuning.
AI.method: Build a visual-action support memory from successful demonstrations. For each proposed action chunk, evaluate visual similarity to the memory and action consistency. Use phase-local support for intra-phase transfers and global support for returning to policy after operator recovery. Calibrate separate switching thresholds via empirical quantiles from held-out expert demonstrations. Retain intervention segments from successful rollouts to guide policy updates.
AI.result: Real-world bimanual manipulation experiments show higher post-adaptation task success and reduced operator-control time compared with manual intervention.
AI.conclusion: AutoIntervene enhances robustness of action-chunking visuomotor policies by enabling selective, phase-aware operator intervention and learning-driven policy updates, improving real-world performance with less manual control.

title: Bend the Basics: Degradation-Aware Deformable Tokenization for All-in-One Image Restoration
summary: All-in-one image restoration seeks a single model that can recover images degraded by diverse and spatially non-uniform corruptions. However, many unified Transformers rely on fixed patch partitioning: task/degradation condition is injected only into the backbone blocks after tokenization, leaving the embedding and reconstruction stages insensitive to local degradation variations. In contrast to previous approaches, we present Flexible Image Transformer (FIT) that explicitly models degradation awareness across the entire pipeline, from patch sampling to pixel reconstruction. Specifically, FIT employs a lightweight Degradation Encoder to predict a global degradation vector $\mathbf{g}$ and a spatial degradation map $\mathbf{M}$ from local degradation severity, which jointly condition the patch embedding and unembedding through adaptive deformation. Moreover, to improve robustness across degradation types, we introduce a task-token dropout strategy that regularizes task conditioning during training. On five standard benchmarks (BSD68, Rain100L, SOTS, GoPro, and LOLv1), FIT achieves state-of-the-art performance with 30.72 dB average PSNR on the five-degradation setting and 32.83 dB on the three-degradation setting, outperforming recent unified restoration methods by +0.5$\sim$1.1 dB. Moreover, the learned offsets provide a direct handle for visualizing degradation-aware spatial adaptation.

AI.tldr: A Transformer-based all-in-one image restoration method (FIT) that models degradation awareness across the entire pipeline via a Degradation Encoder producing global vector g and spatial map M, with adaptive deformation in patch embedding/unembedding, plus task-token dropout; achieves state-of-the-art on five benchmarks with ~0.5-1.1 dB gains.
AI.motivation: Unified restoration across diverse and non-uniform degradations; current methods fix patch partitioning and are insensitive to local degradation; need to propagate degradation conditioning through embedding and reconstruction.
AI.method: Degradation Encoder predicts global degradation vector g and spatial map M from local degradation severity; adaptively deform patch embedding and unembedding; incorporate task-token dropout during training to regularize conditioning.
AI.result: State-of-the-art PSNR: 30.72 dB average on five-degradation, 32.83 dB on three-degradation across five benchmarks (BSD68, Rain100L, SOTS, GoPro, LOLv1); outperform recent unified methods by 0.5–1.1 dB. Learned offsets enable visualization of degradation-aware spatial adaptation.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates effectiveness and interpretability of degradation-aware conditioning across the restoration pipeline, supporting a robust, unified framework with potential for visualization and debugging.

title: The Optimizer Is the Agent: Reasoning-Driven Search across Prompts, Programs, and ML Workflows
summary: Recent systems for optimizing prompts, programs, and ML workflows typically rely on explicit outer-loop controllers such as evolutionary search, bandits, or textual-gradient methods. We ask a fundamentally different question: how much of this search policy can be internalized by a single tool-using agent? We present ReASearch, a unified framework for reasoning-driven optimization in which the agent autonomously decides what to evaluate, how to diagnose failures, which edits to make, and when to verify or restart. Rather than serving only as a proposal generator guided by hand-designed heuristics, the agent actively analyzes outcomes, allocates budget, and refines its strategy over long horizons through persistent memory. With a shared agent loop and domain-specific tools, ReASearch instantiates the exact same scaffold to optimize prompts, programs, and ML workflows. Across 14 diverse tasks, it is competitive with and mostly better than specialized optimization systems, achieving gains of 2% to 40% over strong domain-specific baselines, and in some cases discovering solutions that improve on prior human best-known results. Crucially, we observe that complex search behaviors, which are typically implemented by explicit controllers, emerge naturally from the agent's reasoning process.

AI.tldr: ReASearch enables an autonomous, reasoning-driven agent to internalize search strategies for prompts, programs, and ML workflows, using persistent memory; it achieves competitive or superior results across 14 tasks, with emergent complex search behaviors.
AI.motivation: To move beyond explicit outer-loop controllers (evolutionary search, bandits, textual-gradient methods) by embedding optimization policy inside a single tool-using agent; address long-horizon optimization, budget allocation, and failure diagnosis via persistent memory.
AI.method: A unified framework (ReASearch) with a shared agent loop and domain-specific tools. The agent autonomously decides what to evaluate, how to diagnose failures, which edits to make, and when to verify/restart. It uses persistent memory to refine its strategy over long horizons, and applies the same scaffold to prompts, programs, and ML workflows.
AI.result: Across 14 diverse tasks, ReASearch is competitive with, and mostly better than, specialized optimization systems. It yields gains of 2% to 40% over strong baselines, and in some cases discovers solutions improving on prior human best-known results.
AI.conclusion: Complex search behaviors typically implemented by explicit controllers emerge from the agent’s reasoning. The framework demonstrates that an internalized search policy can generalize across domains (prompts, programs, ML workflows) and reduce reliance on external optimization controllers.

title: Retrofitting Linear Attention into Diffusion Language Models
summary: Diffusion language models (dLLMs) offer a promising alternative to autoregressive models by accelerating inference through parallel decoding. Recent dLLMs commonly use blockwise semi-autoregressive decoding, generating blocks autoregressively while denoising tokens within each active block in parallel. However, despite KV caching, each denoising step still attends to all previous blocks, repeatedly incurring prefix-attention cost. Motivated by this bottleneck, we ask whether dLLM inference can be further accelerated by linearizing attention over previous blocks. We introduce block-hybrid attention, which retains exact softmax attention within the active denoising block while applying linear attention over previous blocks. We show that this hybrid attention can be retrofitted into a pretrained dLLM with minimal post-training: LLaDA-Hybrid replaces 6 of the 20 attention layers in LLaDA~2.1, a 16B open-source dLLM, largely following LoLCAT (Zhang et al, 2024). The conversion takes only approximately 60 hours while preserving benchmark performance: 72.0% vs. 75.6% on HumanEval, 63.0% vs. 57.7% on MBPP+, and 86.7% vs. 88.3% on CMATH. With a Triton implementation, LLaDA-Hybrid achieves up to $1.7\times$ higher decoding throughput and supports more concurrent requests before exhausting memory, showing that pretrained dLLMs can be efficiently linearized for faster inference. Our code is available at: https://github.com/Diuven/LLaDA-Hybrid.

AI.tldr: Hybrid block-hybrid attention for diffusion LLMs: exact softmax within active denoising block and linear attention over previous blocks enable faster inference; retrofit on LLaDA-2.1 (6 of 20 layers) yields up to 1.7x throughput with modest benchmark changes.
AI.motivation: Reduce the prefix-attention bottleneck in blockwise semi-autoregressive diffusion LLMs by linearizing attention across previous blocks while preserving full attention within the current block.
AI.method: Introduce block-hybrid attention. Retrofit into a pretrained dLLM by replacing 6 of 20 attention layers in LLaDA-2.1 (LoLCAT-inspired). Implement with Triton for speed; code release provided. Approximate 60-hour conversion.
AI.result: Up to 1.7x decoding throughput with more concurrent requests. Benchmark performance: HumanEval 72.0% (vs 75.6% baseline), MBPP+ 63.0% (vs 57.7%), CMATH 86.7% (vs 88.3%). Conversion time ~60 hours.
AI.conclusion: Block-hybrid attention demonstrates a practical, near-equivalent-performance pathway to linearize dLLM attention, enabling substantial throughput gains with modest accuracy trade-offs and feasible retrofitting into existing models.

title: M2-SMap: Memory-Efficient Semantic Mapping with Hierarchical Multi-Model Representation
summary: Dense point cloud maps, as a typically used mapping representation, are difficult to deploy on resource-constrained robots because their memory consumption grows rapidly with scene scale. Although compact single-model representations reduce memory cost, their fixed geometric expressiveness is insufficient for structurally diverse environments. Existing multi-model methods improve representational flexibility, yet their feature extraction and model selection are often dominated by local geometry, which can cause overfitting and adhesion between objects. To address these issues, this paper presents M2-SMap, a memory-efficient semantic mapping framework based on hierarchical multi-model representation. First, a hierarchical geometric decomposition partitions RGB-D point clouds into compact Gaussian components. Then, a projection-guided semantic annotation mechanism assigns instance identities to each component. Subsequently, these annotations are incorporated into an object-aware Gaussian fusion strategy. Furthermore, a multi-scale feature extraction strategy separates large planar regions, semantic objects, and complex residual structures, which are respectively represented by bounded planes, object-level superquadrics, and GMM primitives. Experiments on three RGB-D sequences show that M2-SMap runs in real time at no less than 29.37 Hz while achieving the lowest primitive count, with an average reduction of 18.7% over the best baseline. It also reduces the mean per-frame number of measured inter-object adhesion cases from 2.808 to 0, demonstrating efficient and semantically consistent scene representation.

AI.tldr: M2-SMap is a memory-efficient hierarchical multi-model semantic mapping framework that uses Gaussian decomposition and multi-scale features to deliver real-time performance with fewer primitives and improved semantic consistency.
AI.motivation: Dense point-cloud maps demand large memory on resource-constrained robots, and single-model representations lack expressiveness; existing multi-model approaches risk overfitting and object adhesion due to geometry-driven feature extraction.
AI.method: Hierarchical geometric decomposition of RGB-D point clouds into compact Gaussian components; projection-guided semantic annotations to assign instance identities; object-aware Gaussian fusion; multi-scale feature extraction separating planar regions, semantic objects, and complex residuals into bounded planes, superquadrics, and GMM primitives.
AI.result: Real-time performance (≥29.37 Hz); lowest primitive count with ~18.7% average reduction over the best baseline; inter-object adhesion cases reduced from 2.808 to 0 per frame.
AI.conclusion: M2-SMap delivers memory-efficient, semantically consistent scene representations with flexible hierarchical modeling and real-time operation, reducing memory footprint and adhesion while maintaining accuracy.

title: GOPI: Generation-Oriented 3D Pose Inference for Furniture Insertion from Single-View RGB-D Indoor Scenes
summary:
We study the problem of inserting new furniture into indoor scene images. Under masked single-view 2D image-plane conditioning, however, the physical scale of the inserted furniture relative to the scene cannot be uniquely determined, making physically grounded furniture placement underdetermined from image evidence alone. We therefore reformulate the task as a combination of 3D pose inference and geometry-guided image generation, where estimating a geometrically plausible 3D placement is essential for reliable synthesis.
  To this end, we propose a two-stage framework. For 3D placement, we introduce GOPI, a generation-oriented 3D pose inference framework that addresses the underdetermined nature of single-view furniture insertion through data-driven iterative inference, producing geometrically plausible object placements. For image generation, we develop a geometry-guided conditioning strategy that projects the inferred 3D pose into the image plane as a pixel-aligned constraint, enforcing consistency between the synthesized image and the underlying 3D geometry.
  Experimental results validate the proposed framework from both 3D pose estimation and image synthesis perspectives. For 3D placement, GOPI produces poses with stronger geometric feasibility and better consistency with reference layouts than direct regression and vanilla baselines. For image synthesis, our method preserves alignment with the projected 3D geometry across different furniture scales, showing stable projection-generation alignment across the tested furniture scales.

AI.tldr: A two-stage GOPI framework for single-view furniture insertion: iterative 3D pose inference and geometry-guided image synthesis projecting the 3D pose onto the image plane to enforce consistency; results show improved geometric feasibility and scale-consistent synthesis.
AI.motivation: Single-view indoor scenes leave the physical scale of inserted furniture underdetermined, making physically grounded placement difficult.
AI.method: Stage 1: GOPI performs data-driven iterative inference to estimate geometrically plausible 3D placements; Stage 2: geometry-guided image generation uses the projected 3D pose as a pixel-aligned constraint to align synthesis with 3D geometry.
AI.result: GOPI yields poses with stronger geometric feasibility and better consistency with reference layouts than direct regression baselines; image synthesis preserves alignment with projected 3D geometry across different furniture scales, showing stable projection-generation alignment.
AI.conclusion: Combining (i) 3D pose inference to resolve scale underdetermination and (ii) geometry-guided image generation to enforce 3D-to-2D consistency yields improved 3D placement quality and image synthesis fidelity in single-view furniture insertion.

title: bioMoR: Biology-Guided Mixture-of-Recursions for Effective Genomic Learning
summary: Transformer models for high-dimensional omics analysis process thousands of genes or pathways, although only a subset requires deep computation. Mixture-of-Recursions (MoR) improves efficiency through adaptive token-choice or expert-choice routing. We propose bioMoR, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first framework to apply MoR to gene-level and pathway-level learning. Our contributions include identifying three locations for integrating structured biological knowledge within an MoR backbone: graph-based information sharing refines token embeddings, a structural bias guides self-attention toward biologically related tokens, and a graph-aware router uses neighborhood information to determine each token's recursion depth. These techniques are centered on our insight that additional knowledge of token interaction can effectively help models construct embeddings and select which tokens should be learned more deeply. Across eight benchmarks spanning diverse omics data types and evaluated under a unified five-fold cross-validation protocol, bioMoR improves average macro-F1 by 8.2 percentage points and balanced accuracy by 7.1 percentage points over the strongest biology-agnostic MoR baseline while using 75 percent fewer parameters and up to 58 percent fewer FLOPs than a non-recursive Transformer. The selected marker genes or pathways provide biological interpretability, while their token-specific recursion depths reveal how computation is allocated.

AI.tldr: bioMoR extends Mixture-of-Recursions (MoR) to gene- and pathway-level omics learning by integrating structured biological knowledge at embedding, attention bias, and routing stages; achieves strong accuracy and efficiency, with interpretable marker selections and recursion-depth-based computation budgeting.
AI.motivation: High-dimensional omics data pose efficiency and interpretability challenges for Transformers; MoR increases efficiency via adaptive token/expert routing, but biology-agnostic; integrating biological structure can improve embeddings, attention, and computation allocation.
AI.method: Incorporates MoR backbone with three integration points: graph-based information sharing to refine token embeddings; a structural bias to guide self-attention towards biologically related tokens; a graph-aware router to determine token recursion depth using neighborhood information. Evaluated on eight omics benchmarks under five-fold cross-validation; compared to strongest biology-agnostic MoR baseline and non-recursive Transformer.
AI.result: BioMoR yields +8.2 macro-F1 points and +7.1 balanced accuracy on average; uses 75% fewer parameters and up to 58% fewer FLOPs than non-recursive Transformer; selected marker genes/pathways provide interpretability; token-specific recursion depths reveal computation allocation.
AI.conclusion: Integrating structured biological knowledge into MoR improves performance, parameter efficiency, and interpretability in gene- and pathway-level learning across diverse omics data; supports resource-efficient, interpretable deep models for high-dimensional biology.

title: The Sparsity Whisperer
comment: 10 pages, 3 figures. Code available at https://github.com/Shavit-Lab/Whisper
summary: Pruning reduces the inference cost of large language models, but existing criteria primarily preserve large activations or reconstruct layer outputs. We argue that this overlooks a key computation performed by particularly sparsity-sensitive neurons in the MLP up and gate projections: separating similar inputs into dissimilar outputs. This suggests that effective pruning should preserve not only activations, but also the differences between outputs more broadly. We introduce a family of difference-informed pruning methods built upon this principle. Wisp is a first-order, update-free method that scores weights using input-difference norms, and Wisp+ refines this score neuronwise using the input pairs each neuron separates most strongly. Finally, Whisper is a second-order method that uses a lightly regularized difference Hessian as its reconstruction objective. Across Llama 2 and 3.1 models from 7B to 405B parameters, our second-order variant consistently improves over strong reconstruction-based baselines, while our update-free variants improve over activation-aware baselines, especially in constrained settings. The improvements over Wanda and SparseGPT extend to structured sparsity, downstream evaluations, and other model families. Augmenting stronger techniques such as RIA and ALPS with our difference-informed criteria yields further improvements, shifting the overall accuracy-runtime frontier outward at negligible additional cost. These results suggest that preserving output differences is a broadly useful and composable signal for post-training LLM sparsification.

AI.tldr: Difference-informed pruning for LLMs using Wisp (update-free, first-order), Wisp+ (neuronwise refinement), and Whisper (second-order with a difference Hessian). They improve post-training sparsification across Llama 2/3.1 (7B–405B), outperform reconstruction baselines (Wanda/SparseGPT), extend to structured sparsity and other models, and synergize with RIA/ALPS for a better accuracy-runtime frontier at negligible cost.
AI.motivation: Standard pruning criteria emphasize large activations or reconstructing layer outputs, ignoring a key computation: sparsity-sensitive neurons in MLP up- and gate-projections separate similar inputs into dissimilar outputs. Preserving output differences may better retain the functional computations during pruning.
AI.method: Introduce a family of difference-informed pruning methods. Wisp is a first-order, update-free score based on input-difference norms. Wisp+ refines these scores neuronwise by considering the input pairs each neuron separates most strongly. Whisper is a second-order method using a lightly regularized difference Hessian as the reconstruction objective. Evaluation spans Llama 2 and 3.1 models from 7B to 405B parameters, including structured sparsity and other model families; further augmented with RIA and ALPS.
AI.result: The second-order Whisper consistently surpasses strong reconstruction-based baselines. The update-free Wisp and Wisp+ outperform activation-aware baselines, especially under constrained sparsity. Improvements extend to Wanda and SparseGPT and carry over to structured sparsity, downstream tasks, and other model families. Integrating with RIA/ALPS yields further gains, expanding the accuracy-runtime frontier with negligible cost.
AI.conclusion: Preserving output differences is a broadly useful, composable signal for post-training LLM sparsification, enabling more effective pruning across model scales and families.

title: Detection and Ranging of Transient Extrinsic Contacts Based on 6D Dynamic Tactile Sensing
summary: Delicate manipulation often involves transient and subtle collisions between a grasped object and the environment. While the human hand localizes these contacts effortlessly thanks to superior tactile sensitivity, robotic systems often lack the requisite resolution to acquire the information necessary for motion planning, resulting in clumsy manipulation or even task failure. Here, we propose transient extrinsic contact detection and ranging (TECDAR), a simple yet fast and efficient method for detecting and ranging extrinsic contact of grasped objects. Our design of gripper tips employs dynamic tactile sensing leveraging a single 2.5$\times$3 mm 6D inertial measurement unit. The sensor captures sub-millisecond tip deformations at a 7 kHz sampling rate, but operating on a data stream of only 84 KB/s. High bandwidth and compact data size enable the system to rapidly detect and localize contact between grasped objects and their surroundings. Specifically, fusing tactile data with robot pose via an extended Kalman filter enables fast and precise localization of extrinsic contact, reaching millimeter-level accuracy within 180 ms. Experimental results demonstrate that the system achieves an average localization accuracy of approximately 7\,mm in both line-contact and point-contact localization tasks. Furthermore, this near-instantaneous localization enables the robot to rectify its trajectory on a millisecond scale, facilitating precise tool manipulation and enhanced perception of complex environments purely through tactile exploration and mapping. We envision such techniques advancing the future of robotics across domains requiring delicate manipulation, including precision assembly, surgical assistance, and autonomous exploration in touch-dominant environments. Project page: humitlab.github.io/TECDAR/

AI.tldr: TECDAR offers fast, high-bandwidth tactile-based extrinsic contact detection and ranging using a tiny IMU-equipped gripper tip, fused with pose via EKF to localize contact with ~7 mm accuracy in ~180 ms, enabling precise trajectory rectification and tactile mapping.
AI.motivation: Enable reliable manipulation of delicate objects by detecting and localizing extrinsic contacts that are transient and subtle, overcoming limited tactile resolution in robots.
AI.method: Integrate a 2.5x3 mm 6D IMU-based tactile sensor on gripper tips, sample at 7 kHz with 84 KB/s data; fuse tactile signals with robot pose using an extended Kalman filter to estimate the extrinsic contact location.
AI.result: Achieves ~7 mm average localization accuracy for line and point contact; localization within 180 ms; enables millisecond-scale trajectory correction; demonstrates improved precision in tactile exploration and mapping.
AI.conclusion: TECDAR provides a simple, fast, efficient pathway for tactile-based extrinsic contact detection, with potential impact on precision assembly, surgical assistance, and touch-dominant robotic exploration.

title: ECAD: Expanding Class-Agnostic Detection Beyond Thing-Centric Objectness
summary: Object detection is a fundamental task in visual perception, providing structured region representations for recognition, grounding, reasoning, and interaction. However, existing detection paradigms largely inherit a thing-centric notion of objectness, where detectors are mainly trained to localize discrete and countable object instances. Consequently, many semantically meaningful visual elements, such as sky, road, grassland, water, and sports courts, are often absorbed into the background despite their importance for scene understanding and spatial reasoning. In this paper, we formulate Expanded Class-Agnostic Detection (ECAD), a new setting that aims to discover category-agnostic visual candidates beyond conventional thing-centric objects. To support this setting, we construct BTCO-Bench, a Beyond Thing-Centric Objectness benchmark with category-agnostic box annotations covering both real-world and cross-domain scenarios. We further propose ECADet, a lightweight DETR-based detector built upon a frozen DINOv3 encoder, and introduce Geometry-Aware Expert Regression (GAER) and Prototype-Guided Query Modulation (PGQM) to improve localization and objectness estimation for diverse visual elements, respectively. Extensive experiments show that ECADet consistently outperforms representative class-agnostic and proposal-based detectors on BTCO-Bench, demonstrating the effectiveness of expanded objectness discovery. Code and benchmark will be released.

AI.tldr: Proposes Expanded Class-Agnostic Detection (ECAD) to discover category-agnostic visual elements beyond traditional objectness, via BTCO-Bench and ECADet (DETR-based) with GAER and PGQM, achieving improved detection on diverse visual elements.
AI.motivation: Current detectors favor thing-centric objectness and struggle to model semantically meaningful non-object visual elements (e.g., sky, road, water), hindering scene understanding and spatial reasoning.
AI.method: Introduce ECAD setting and BTCO-Bench with category-agnostic box annotations. Develop ECADet, a lightweight DETR-based detector using a frozen DINOv3 encoder, with two novel components: Geometry-Aware Expert Regression (GAER) for improved localization, and Prototype-Guided Query Modulation (PGQM) for better objectness estimation of diverse visual elements.
AI.result: ECADet consistently outperforms representative class-agnostic and proposal-based detectors on BTCO-Bench, demonstrating the effectiveness of expanded objectness discovery.
AI.conclusion: Expanded objectness discovery is viable and beneficial for capturing diverse, non-thing visual elements; the BTCO-Bench and ECADet will be released to facilitate research in this direction.

title: From Cheap Fakes to Pure Synthesis: Addressing the New Era of T2V Fake News Videos
summary: Recent text-to-video (T2V) generation models enable fake news videos to be synthesized from scratch, shifting the threat beyond cheap fakes assembled from existing footage. Such news videos can closely match fabricated narratives, creating a modality alignment trap for existing detectors. Existing datasets lack pure synthesis fake news videos. Although directly prompting T2V models with descriptions of fake news videos can yield perfectly aligned samples, it reduces the fake news video detection (FNVD) to unimodal shortcuts and causes semantic-visual degeneration. To counter this, we formulate T2V-FNVD as a novel ternary classification task with three labels (real, cheap fake, and pure synthesis fake) and construct the first pure synthesis fake news video dataset (PS-FNVD). PS-FNVD includes fabricated events with aligned deception (Type 1) and true events with false visual provenance (Type 2), preventing models from exploiting unimodal shortcuts. Furthermore, we propose the Reasoning-guided T2V-FNVD (R-T2V) framework. Trained through conditioned rationale generation and supervised fine-tuning, R-T2V integrates high-level semantic logic with low-level physical generative traces to predict the ternary veracity label. Extensive experiments across 10 prevailing baselines show that R-T2V achieves the state-of-the-art performance, outperforming the second-best baseline by 12.20 percentage points in accuracy and 8.46 percentage points in macro $F_1$.

AI.tldr: A ternary M-classification approach for T2V-based fake news video detection, introducing PS-FNVD (pure synthesis fakes dataset) with Type 1 and Type 2 deception, and R-T2V (Reasoning-guided T2V-FNVD) that uses conditioned rationale generation and fine-tuning to achieve state-of-the-art results across baselines.
AI.motivation: Addresses the emerging risk of pure synthesis fake news videos generated by text-to-video models. Existing datasets lack pure synthesis fakes, and prompting models with fake descriptions risks unimodal shortcuts and semantic-visual degeneration. A ternary task with a dedicated dataset and reasoning-based method aims to improve robustness.
AI.method: Formulate T2V-FNVD as a three-way (real, cheap fake, pure synthesis fake) classification task. Construct PS-FNVD with Type 1 (fabricated events with aligned deception) and Type 2 (true events with false visual provenance). Propose R-T2V, which is trained with conditioned rationale generation and supervised fine-tuning to fuse high-level semantic logic with low-level generative traces for ternary veracity prediction.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across 10 prevailing baselines show R-T2V achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming the second-best baseline by 12.20 percentage points in accuracy and 8.46 percentage points in macro F1.
AI.conclusion: The combination of a purpose-built dataset (PS-FNVD) and a reasoning-guided framework (R-T2V) mitigates unimodal shortcuts and enhances detection of pure synthesis fake news videos, demonstrating substantial gains over existing approaches.

title: Cryptanalytic Extraction of Isolated Bias-Free GLU Feed-Forward Blocks by Antipodal Separation
summary: Cryptanalytic extraction has been demonstrated for ReLU networks, for networks using componentwise activations such as GELU or SiLU, and for a Transformer's final projection matrix. These methods do not recover the bias-free Gated Linear Unit (GLU) feed-forward blocks used in many modern language models. Such a block multiplies an activated linear projection by a second learned linear projection within each hidden unit, a two-branch structure absent from the network classes and final-layer setting addressed by those methods. We give a constructive, multi-stage forward-query recovery primitive for isolated bias-free GLU blocks. Finite-difference curvature supplies gate-direction candidates, and paired observations at x and -x separate gate magnitude, orientation, and value-branch coupling. Across high-precision targets, six Qwen layers, an 8,192-unit Llama subproblem, and a full-dimensional Gemma block all reach sub-percent median validation error. Four finite-precision configurations remain below 5 percent median error, but none reproduces every stored weight. These isolated-block experiments are not an end-to-end model-API attack: deriving the required internal block responses from final model outputs remains unsolved.

AI.tldr: Proposes a forward-query recovery method for bias-free GLU feed-forward blocks in transformers, using finite-difference curvature and x vs -x observations to recover gate and value-branch parameters; achieves sub-percent to ~5% median error on various high-dimensional blocks but not perfect weight recovery; not an end-to-end model-API attack.
AI.motivation: GLU blocks with two-branch gating inside hidden units are common in modern LMs but have not been targeted by cryptanalytic weight-recovery methods. The work aims to recover internal GLU parameters from external block behavior, addressing a gap in the security/interpretability literature.
AI.method: A multi-stage forward-query recovery primitive for isolated bias-free GLU blocks. Uses finite-difference curvature to generate gate-direction candidates and pairs observations at inputs x and -x to separate gate magnitude, orientation, and coupling between the two branches. Tested on high-dimensional blocks (six Qwen layers, an 8,192-unit Llama subproblem, Gemma block).
AI.result: High-precision targets yield sub-percent median validation error in recovered parameters. Four finite-precision configurations yield median error below 5%, but none perfectly reproduces all stored weights.
AI.conclusion: These experiments isolate a GLU block and do not constitute an end-to-end model-API attack, since deriving the full chain of internal block responses from final-output behavior remains unsolved. The work marks progress in block-level cryptanalytic recovery but highlights remaining challenges for complete weight extraction.

title: LifelongCrossNav: Persistent 3D Semantic Memory for Cross-Floor Multi-Object Navigation
